story: Completing time-of-day expressions in opening-hours listings, predicting 'pm', 'am', or the '30' of a half-hour after a digit, usually copying the format of times seen earlier in the same listing.

Predicting the recurring punctuation and connectives (commas, hyphens, 'and', semicolons) that glue together the guidebook's formulaic list-style entries, repeating separators already used earlier in the passage.

Completing well-known multi-token proper names and all-caps section labels from their first piece (TOUR->IST, Tottenham -> Court, Oliver -> Twist, TAX->I), without needing the name to have appeared earlier.
Continuing rare or unusual words mid-token from a subword fragment (Pim->lic, So->ane, bo->hem, spic->-, Market S->q), spelling out names and words the tokenizer split into pieces.
Continuing boilerplate templates the passage has already used many times, chiefly ' MAP' after 'GOOG-LE' and the '.' inside website addresses like www.venuename[.]co.uk.
Predicting the newline that ends a guidebook listing line right after its closing parenthesis (opening hours, tube station, etc.), late in the window where many such lines have already occurred.
Predicting the period inside a clock time (as in 5.30pm or 10.30am) immediately after the hour digit in opening-hours listings.
Continuing partially-spelled British place names and uncommon words mid-word (Picc->ad, Portob->ello, Cotsw->olds, stradd->ling, gris->ly), completing the next subword piece.
Continuing stock guidebook phrases at their fixed next word, such as 'Located in', 'housed in', and the hyphen of 'Mon-Sat' day ranges.
Completing familiar British compound place names from their first word (High -> St, Hyde -> Park, Hampton -> Court, Primrose -> Hill), from stored knowledge rather than by copying the context.

Filling in the fixed pieces of listing boilerplate by copying its template from earlier in the passage: G->OO in GOOGLE, 'am' after the opening hour, and day names after '-' or '&' in ranges like Mon-Sat and Sat & Sun.
Predicting the article 'the' or 'a' (or another function word) that starts a noun phrase right after a verb or preposition in ordinary descriptive prose.
Late in the window, copying names already seen in the passage into website addresses and boilerplate (predicting the '.' or 'uk' of www.venuename.co.uk after the venue was named just above).
Predicting the newline that closes a listing's parenthesized info line (hours, prices, tube stop) right after the closing parenthesis, relatively early in the window.
Predicting the period or comma that closes a descriptive clause at its final noun or verb (…whenever the sun shines[.], …best bars and nightlife[.]) in flowing historical or scene-setting prose.
Predicting the small linking words (and, in, or, this) that join clauses and noun phrases mid-sentence in long descriptive passages, typically after a comma, article, or possessive.
